capsules_info.title: About your lightning capsules
capsules_info.why_body_1: Your Bark balance is held as a collection of small lightning capsules (VTXOs). Each capsule has an expiry date. To keep your funds fully self-custodial, meaning you can always recover them yourself without needing the Second.tech server's permission, each capsule must be refreshed before it expires.
capsules_info.why_body_2: If a capsule expires without being refreshed, the Second.tech server can sweep the funds at any time. Recovery after expiry is not guaranteed, so treat the expiry date as a hard deadline.
capsules_info.why_body_3: Keeping capsules refreshed also pays off if you ever run an Emergency Exit: fresh capsules make the exit cheaper in fees, faster to settle, and more private.
capsules_info.reminders_title: How reminders keep your capsules safe
capsules_info.reminders_body_1: Cypher Box sends up to 6 reminder notifications before any lightning capsule expires. The schedule is fixed: 7 days, 4 days, 2 days, 24 hours, 12 hours, and 6 hours before expiry. Each one escalates in urgency. The two earliest exist so you still have time to exit on chain if you need to, which takes longer than a refresh.
capsules_info.reminders_body_2: Tap any reminder and Cypher Box opens directly on the Capsules tab, works out which capsules need refreshing, and shows you the fee before anything is spent. You do not need to find a button or pick capsules yourself. Tap Refresh on that summary to go ahead, or Cancel to leave the capsules as they are.
capsules_info.reminders_body_3: The Reminders toggle lives in two places: at the bottom of the Bark Vault Created screen when you first create your wallet, and on the Vault tab inside the Bark vault menu. Default is on. If you turn it off, no reminders fire and you alone are responsible for opening the app and refreshing your capsules before they expire.
capsules_info.reminders_body_4: The reminders are your safety net. Refreshing only works while the app is open, so tapping a reminder is what keeps your capsules alive.
capsules_info.spendable_title: Your balance stays spendable while it refreshes
capsules_info.spendable_body_1: Refreshing no longer locks your funds. When a capsule is refreshing, including the automatic step right after you receive over Lightning, you can keep spending it the whole time. There is no waiting for the refresh to finish before your balance is usable.
capsules_info.spendable_body_2: A refresh usually finishes within about an hour and gives the capsule a fresh full life. Just leave the app running until it completes.
capsules_info.color_yellow_body: Past the midpoint. Worth refreshing next time you're in the app.
capsules_info.color_orange_body: Within the refresh window. Refresh it now, before the reminders start.
capsules_info.color_red_body: Needs refresh now. Reminders are firing, tap one to refresh. After it expires, the server can claim the capsule.
capsules_info.status_backed_up_body: Spendable, and fully under your control. You can always recover it on-chain yourself. This is the everyday state.
capsules_info.status_refreshing_body: Being given a fresh full life. It stays spendable the whole time, usually under an hour, so you can keep using it while it refreshes.
capsules_info.status_in_flight_body: Being used in another operation: an outgoing send, withdrawal, or boarding. Briefly locked until that operation completes.
capsules_info.dust_body_1: A capsule at or below 500 sats is too small to refresh on its own, so the network will not let it renew alone. To keep dust alive, tap Dust refresh on the capsule: it batches several tiny capsules together, so their combined size clears the minimum, and consolidates them into one healthy capsule.
capsules_info.dust_body_2: Because the amounts are tiny, the fee for a dust batch can sometimes be close to or more than the dust itself, so it is a judgment call. If it is not worth it, just spend the dust as part of a normal payment before it expires. Receiving at least about 700 sats at a time avoids dust in the first place.
capsules_info.fees_body_1: These are the fees the Bark server charges. The refresh fee depends on how much time is left before a capsule expires, not on how old the capsule is. The closer to expiry, the cheaper the refresh.
capsules_info.fees_body_2: Second.tech sets these fees, not Cypher Box, and can change them at any time. The figures below were checked in September 2026. For the current schedule, see:
capsules_info.fee_receive_ln_body: 0%, free. The capsule you receive still has to be refreshed to extend its life by about 28 days, and that costs the refresh fee below.
capsules_info.fee_refresh_body: Free with under 2 days left, 0.2% from 2 to 7 days, 0.4% from 7 to 14 days, and 0.5% with more than 14 days left. A fresh capsule lasts about 28 days, so refreshing one that still has most of its life left costs the most. Waiting for a reminder is cheaper than refreshing on sight.
capsules_info.fee_send_ln_body: 0.2% to 0.5% of the amount, with a 20-sat minimum.
capsules_info.fee_withdraw_body: 0.2% to 0.5% of the amount, plus standard Bitcoin network fees for the on-chain transaction.
capsules_info.tip_body_1: Refreshing late is cheaper. Refreshing early leaves you more room to get out on your own. That is the whole trade.
capsules_info.tip_body_2: If the Second.tech server ever becomes unreachable, you can still recover your sats yourself with an Emergency Exit, straight to the blockchain, without the server's permission. That exit has to be started before the capsule expires, and it needs at least a day to complete.
capsules_info.tip_body_3: So refreshing in the free window, the last 2 days, costs nothing but leaves very little room if the server goes down right then. Refreshing with 2 to 7 days left costs 0.2% and keeps several days of exit room in hand. Refreshing earlier than that costs 0.4% to 0.5% for time the capsule already had.
capsules_info.tip_body_4: The middle is usually the right call, and it is where the reminders start.
capsules_info.tip_body_5: Cypher Box does this part for you. Whenever the app is open it refreshes any capsule with between 28 hours and one week of life left, which is the free and 0.2% part of that table. It never pays the 0.4% or 0.5% bands on your behalf.
capsules_info.tip_body_6: It stops at 28 hours on purpose. Any closer to expiry and a refresh that stalls could eat the day you would need to exit on your own, so the wallet leaves the capsule alone and warns you instead. Capsules under 500 sats are too small to refresh this way and are handled separately.
capsules_info.example_intro: Alex adds 100K sats at the end of every week for 10 weeks, then withdraws the full 1 million sats to cold storage. Using the fees above:
capsules_info.example_receive_body: Free over Lightning or on-chain. An on-chain deposit still pays the normal Bitcoin network fee to arrive.
capsules_info.example_deposit_title: Making each deposit last: about 2,000 sats
capsules_info.example_deposit_body: A Lightning deposit arrives as a short-lived capsule, good for only a few days. The wallet refreshes it straight away to buy the full 28 days. Because the fee tracks the time left on a capsule, that first refresh is a cheap one: free if the capsule arrives with under 2 days on it, otherwise 0.2%, about 200 sats per 100K deposit. Ten deposits, about 2,000 sats. Refreshing a second time right after pays the 0.5% band, because by then the capsule has its full 28 days again.
capsules_info.example_keep_alive_body: After that, a capsule only needs refreshing once every 24 days, and refreshing at the reminder costs 0.2%, or 200 sats per 100K. Across the 10 weeks that is 7 more refreshes.
capsules_info.example_withdraw_body: 0.2% to 0.5% of the 1M sats, depending on how much life the capsules have left, plus a few hundred sats of Bitcoin network fee.
capsules_info.example_total_body: About 0.55% to 0.85% of the 1M sats UTXO going to cold storage.
capsules_info.example_outro: That first refresh on each deposit is automatic and unavoidable, otherwise the capsule expires within days. The later ones are where Alex has a choice, and two habits keep him at the low end: let the reminder tell him when to refresh instead of refreshing on sight, and time the withdrawal for when his capsules are in their last week rather than just after a refresh. Both still leave him several days to exit on his own if the Second.tech server goes down.

checking_login.intro: Pick a provider to power Lightning send/receive. Custodial accounts hold your bitcoin with a third party, while non-custodial wallets let you have full control over your keys and funds.
checking_login.non_custodial_subtitle: Create a self-custodial wallet. Keys under your full control.

checking_intro.title: Lightning Account
checking_intro.body: To use Bitcoin efficiently, you can create a Lightning Account at a reliable custodian. This entity will help you send and receive payments globally, instantaneously, with ~zero fees. You can also use it to accumulate a measured amount of bitcoin until you are able to economically withdraw to self-custody.
checking_intro.caution: Be careful: while bitcoin custodians and exchanges offer user friendly financial services, it's wise to exercise caution with the amount of money you entrust to them. As your balance increases, Cypher Box will notify you and provide instructions on how to secure your wealth independently, without the reliance on any third party custodian.

create_ark.reset_title: Reset Ark wallet on this device?
create_ark.reset_body:
This deletes the wallet's local state AND removes the seed phrase from your Keychain.

Without your written-down seed phrase AND your encrypted .cbark backup file, any funds in this wallet become permanently unrecoverable.

Only continue if:
• You don't own this wallet (e.g. previous device owner), OR
• You've written down your seed AND saved your backup file elsewhere
create_ark.last_chance_body: Tap 'Reset & wipe' to permanently delete the Ark wallet state on this device. This cannot be undone from inside the app.
create_ark.exists_body_1: An Ark wallet was found on this device. Open it to resume using the seed in your Keychain.
create_ark.exists_body_2: If this wallet isn't yours, or the seed no longer matches, tap Reset to delete everything and start over.
create_ark.experimental_body: Ark is a new Bitcoin Layer 2 protocol (by Second.tech). It enables cheap non-custodial Lightning-style payments. The SDK is still pre-1.0, so treat it as experimental.
create_ark.recovery_body: Recovery always needs your seed phrase. Your backup file (.cbark) is encrypted with that seed, so it can never restore anything on its own, and it brings back capsule state the server scan can miss. Keep both, and never lose the seed.

create_ark.bullet_receive: • Can receive Lightning payments and on-chain deposits (board).

ark_seed.saved_q_title: Did you save the backup file?
ark_seed.saved_q_body:
The .cbark file is encrypted with your seed phrase, safe to keep in iCloud Drive, email to yourself, or any cloud storage. Without this file plus your seed, your Bark balance can't be fully recovered.

The best path is to enable iCloud Drive for Cypher Box (iOS Settings → [your name] → iCloud → iCloud Drive → Cypher Box). Cypher Box will then keep an encrypted copy current in your iCloud Drive automatically. Until you do that, re-export from the reminder banner in Bark Settings → Bark Backup after every Lightning receive.

ark_seed.tap_to_reveal: Tap to reveal your seed phrase
ark_seed.backup_section_desc: Can be stored and auto-updated on this device and on your cloud. Each time you send or receive, an encrypted snapshot updates in {location}. That covers app reinstalls and data corruption.
ark_seed.ios_location: Files → On My iPhone → Cypher Box
ark_seed.lose_phone: Lose the phone, though, and the local file goes with it. Your seed can still restore the wallet, but an off-device copy brings back capsule state the server scan can miss:
ark_seed.android_option_label: Optional: sync backup to Google Drive
ark_seed.ios_option_detail: Opens the share sheet so you can save the encrypted ark-backup file. We recommend saving inside iCloud Drive, so Cypher Box keeps it current automatically as your VTXO capsules change. Anywhere else (email, AirDrop, local Files) works for recovery too, but you'll need to re-export after every Lightning receive. Whoever stores it sees ciphertext only.
ark_seed.android_option_detail: Connects your Google account and uploads your ark-backup file to Drive's appDataFolder, hidden from the main Drive UI, only Cypher Box can read it. Updates upload automatically as your VTXO capsules change. Google sees only ciphertext.
ark_seed.folder_option_label: Save to a folder on this phone (auto-updates)
ark_seed.folder_option_detail: Pick a folder you control, for example Internal Storage → Documents → Backups. The encrypted file is written there whenever your wallet changes, and unlike the app's private storage it {survives}. Whatever stores it sees ciphertext only.
ark_seed.save_before_body: Your seed phrase restores the wallet, and the server returns the capsules it still tracks for it. That scan is not guaranteed to find everything, and the backup file is what covers the rest. Pick any one option above before creating the wallet.

recover_ark.nothing_left_title: Wallet recovered, nothing left to restore
recover_ark.nothing_left_body: The Ark server's capsules for this seed were already spent or exited on-chain, so there was nothing to bring back. Your wallet is open and usable.
recover_ark.already_open_title: An Ark wallet is already open
recover_ark.already_open_body: There's a live Ark wallet on this device. Open the setup screen and reset it there first, then recover from your seed. Nothing has been changed.
recover_ark.reopened_body: This device already had this wallet's data, so it was reopened as it was. Nothing was deleted and nothing was re-downloaded.

recover_ark.different_data_body: The Ark data on this device belongs to a different seed phrase, so it can't be reopened with the words you typed. Recovering replaces it. If that other wallet still holds funds, make sure its seed phrase is written down before you continue.

recover_ark.seed_not_saved_continue: This device has no fingerprint set up, so the seed was not stored behind one. Recovery continues. Keep your 12 words safe, you will need them next time.
recover_ark.seed_not_saved_reason: The seed couldn't be saved to this device ({reason}). Your wallet is recovered and usable. Keep your 12 words safe, you will need them next time.
recover_ark.choose_body:
Your Ark seed phrase is in this device's Keychain, so you don't need to type it. Tap unlock below to load the seed via {biometric} / passcode.

Restoring from your ark-backup file, from {cloud} (if you connected it earlier) or a manual export, is the most complete option.

recover_ark.type_body_2: Your ark-backup file restores the most, so use the buttons below if you have one. Without it you can continue with the seed alone. Cypher Box checks the Ark server for capsules linked to your seed and brings back what it finds: all of them, some, or none.

ark_settings.auto_refresh_off_message: Cypher Box will stop refreshing your capsules for you, so you will need to open the app and refresh them yourself. Leave at least two days before a capsule expires. An emergency exit has to confirm on the Bitcoin network before expiry, so acting in the final hours can leave you with no way out.
ark_settings.auto_refresh_off_reminders_off: Reminders are off as well, so nothing will warn you.
ark_settings.auto_refresh_off_reminders_on: Reminders stay on and will still warn you at 2 days, 24 hours, 12 hours and 6 hours.
ark_settings.notif_permission_message: Cypher Box cannot warn you before a capsule expires until notifications are allowed for it in system settings.
ark_settings.drive_disconnect_message: Your existing backup file will stay in Drive. Disconnecting only stops future uploads. You can reconnect any time.
ark_settings.icloud_enable_message: Cypher Box stores its backup in your Documents folder. To sync it to iCloud, open iOS Settings → [your name] → iCloud → iCloud Drive, then enable Cypher Box in the app list.

ark_settings.icloud_not_on_message: Open iOS Settings → [your name] → iCloud → iCloud Drive → scroll the app list and switch Cypher Box ON. Then come back here and tap 'iCloud Drive is on, dismiss' again.

ark_settings.deleted_seed_kept: Backup verified. Ark vault deleted. Seed kept on device for biometric recovery.
ark_settings.deleted: Backup verified. Ark vault deleted from this device.
ark_settings.reminders_blocked: ⚠ Reminders are blocked. You turned them on, but notifications are not allowed for Cypher Box in system settings, so none will arrive. Tap the switch to fix this.
ark_settings.reminders_on_desc: Cypher Box sends 6 reminders before any capsule expires (7 days, 4 days, 2 days, 24 hours, 12 hours, and 6 hours before). Without a refresh, recovery is not guaranteed once a capsule expires.
ark_settings.reminders_off_desc: ⚠ Reminders are OFF. You must open Cypher Box yourself and refresh capsules before they expire. Once a capsule expires, recovery is not guaranteed.
ark_settings.auto_refresh_label: Refresh VTXOs when app is open
ark_settings.auto_refresh_on_desc: While Cypher Box is open, capsules nearing expiry (7 days or below) are refreshed for you and cost 0.2% in fees. Refreshing is free in the last two days, but waiting that long risks losing the exit window if the ASP goes offline.
ark_settings.auto_refresh_off_desc: ⚠ Automatic refresh is OFF. Capsules are now only refreshed inside their last two days, where the server charges no fee. That leaves less room to react if a refresh fails, so refresh earlier yourself if you want more exit runway.
ark_settings.seed_write_down: Write these 12 words on paper and store them somewhere safe. We cannot recover them for you.
ark_settings.seed_keep_backup_file: Keep the Bark backup file (2/2) below as well. The seed restores the wallet, the file covers capsules the server scan can miss.
ark_settings.reexport_body: When you created this wallet, you saved a one-time snapshot of the encrypted backup file. That file doesn't auto-update unless iCloud Drive is on for Cypher Box. Tap "Re-export now" after every Lightning receive, or enable iCloud Drive for Cypher Box and this reminder will go away.
ark_settings.backup_also_need_seed: You also need your seed phrase (1/2) above. The Bark backup file alone is not enough.
ark_settings.local_path_ios: Files → On My iPhone → Cypher Box
ark_settings.local_save_direct: Saved via direct write (atomic move unavailable on this build).
ark_settings.delete_body: This wipes your Ark wallet from this device. The local database with your VTXO capsules. To restore funds you'll still need your {file}.
ark_settings.delete_exit_in_progress_title: ⚠ An Emergency Exit is in progress
ark_settings.delete_exit_in_progress_body: Deleting now stops it. Transactions already on the chain stay there, but nothing will move the rest along until you restore from your ark-backup file. Restore soon, because capsules can expire while an exit is paused.
ark_settings.keep_seed_on_device: Keep seedphrase stored on device for future {biometric} recovery
ark_settings.delete_seed_warning_title: ⚠ Make sure you have your 12-word seed phrase
ark_settings.delete_seed_warning_body: Without the seed AND your ark-backup file, this wallet's funds become unrecoverable.

cold_vault_intro.title: Cold Storage
cold_vault_intro.para_1: For enhanced security, we recommend setting up the Cold Storage Vault where the cryptographic keys that secure it are isolated from internet.
cold_vault_intro.para_2: The Hot Vault offers moderate security suitable for medium-term savings, while the Cold Vault is much more robust and is used for long term savings.
cold_vault_intro.para_3: Your Hot and Cold Vaults can work in conjunction. You can use your Hot Vault as a heating funnel that melts your small capsules and transfer them to your Cold Vault as a single large consolidated cold capsule thereby reducing future fee costs (UTXO consolidation).

cold_vault_intro2.title: Cold Storage
cold_vault_intro2.para_1: To create a Cold Storage Vault you need a signing device: a hardware wallet, or a spare phone kept offline with Cypher Box as your signing wallet. It will create a new key and give you a backup copy in case you lose access to it. The backup looks like a series of 12 or 24 words. You need to write them down on a piece of paper or a steel plate to increase the durability and resilience of your backups.
cold_vault_intro2.guide_sentence: This {guide} can help you choose between our most recommended Bitcoin wallets, sorted by security, price and ease of use, and how to connect them to Cypher Box. It also contains security tips and discount links.

saving_vault_created.cold_para_1: Remember to keep your seed phrase safe, it's your responsibility! This Cold Vault is watch & broadcast only: it shows your balance, gives you addresses to receive on, prepares transactions and broadcasts them once signed. Signing happens on your signing device: a hardware wallet, or an offline phone with Cypher Box as your signing wallet.
saving_vault_created.cold_warning: ⚠️ DO NOT use any of its addresses without checking them on your signing device!
saving_vault_created.cold_para_3: When Bitcoin Network fees become moderately low, you can select the capsules accumulated in your Hot Vault and transfer them to your Cold Storage Vault using the “Move to Cold Vault” button.
saving_vault_created.seed_reminder: Remember to keep your seed phrase safe, it's your responsibility!
saving_vault_created.hot_para_2: Each slot represents a materialized Bitcoin capsule (UTXO). You can tap inside the vault to browse its addresses, capsules, transaction history, seed phrase, and so on.
saving_vault_created.hot_para_3: It's recommended that you deposit small to medium sized capsules, and once network fees are low, you can either move them to your Cold Vault, or 'consolidate' them together to save on future network fees.
saving_vault_created.seed_next_1: Next, on the signer: make a SeedQR backup, give your watch-only wallet this seed's public key and check the first addresses match.
saving_vault_created.seed_next_2: Then wipe the seed from this phone, and sign by scanning the SeedQR.

saving_vault_intro_new.title: Savings Vault
saving_vault_intro_new.warning: {careful} This feature is highly advanced and may lead to a loss of access to your funds. Cypher Box will gradually guide you through proper security measures and allow you to create vaults as you progress in your bitcoin journey.

adjust_hot_threshold.title: Hot Storage Threshold
adjust_hot_threshold.desc_1: This threshold prompts reminder to transfer your coins from your hot Savings Vault to your Cold Storage Vault after accumulating a certain number of coins.
adjust_hot_threshold.desc_2: By storing a measured number of coins in your hot wallet up to this limit, you allow yourself to securely hold bitcoin that can easily be liquidated and moved back to your Lightning Account for quick spending, striking a balance between efficiency and security.
adjust_hot_threshold.desc_3: Exceeding this threshold increases the risk associated with prolonged exposure of your funds to online threats since the keys to your Savings Vault are not isolated from the internet like the keys to your Cold Storage Vault.
adjust_hot_threshold.desc_4: Conversely, decreasing the threshold enhances security by reducing the time your coins remain in a hot vault, but it will result in more frequent cold storage rounds and fewer coins (UTXOs) moved to your cold vault. As you consider adjusting the threshold, it's essential to weigh the trade-offs between convenience and security, ensuring that your decision aligns with your risk tolerance and operational preferences.
adjust_hot_threshold.beyond_number: You can store coins beyond this number!

threshold_adjust.title: Withdrawal Threshold
threshold_adjust.intro: You can adjust the threshold at which you can withdraw and materialize the money accumulated on your Lightning Account.
threshold_adjust.balance_warning: Be aware that adjusting this threshold involves balancing Bitcoin network fees against counter-party risk:
threshold_adjust.increase_desc: Increasing the threshold will reduce the percentage fee for withdrawals but it may introduce greater counter-party risk since funds in your Lightning Account are maintained by a centralized custodian. A higher threshold means your assets are under their control for an extended period, increasing the risk associated with their custody.
threshold_adjust.decrease_desc: Decreasing the threshold may reduce counter-party risk but will result in a higher percentage fee for withdrawals
threshold_adjust.coin_size_note: Note that this threshold will determine the size of each coin you will secure later in your Savings Vault and a small threshold may lead to a greater number of coins (UTXOs) which can also elevate the fees for future on-chain transactions, such as when transferring your coins to Cold Storage.
threshold_adjust.reserve_note: You should also consider setting aside a ‘Reserve Amount’ which is an amount to be left in your Lightning Account after the settlement is completed. This will help you retain the ability to send and spend bitcoin cheaply using the Lightning Network.

saving_vault_intro.title: Hot Savings Vault
saving_vault_intro.para_1: Hot Vault, commonly known as a ‘hot wallet’, allows you to become the sole owner of your bitcoin, as the saying goes: Not your keys, not your coins. Money stored in this vault will be secured by the main Bitcoin network, not by a third party custodian.
saving_vault_intro.para_2: To create a Hot Vault, you first need to generate your keys: your phone will create the private key, encrypt it, and store it in its memory. It will also create a backup copy (12 words), just in case you lose access to your phone.
saving_vault_intro.para_3: Caution: while it offers a much more secure storage environment than the Lightning Account, the keys to your Hot Vault are generated and stored on an internet-connected device. As your balance and technical skills increase, you should think about investing in an offline hardware signing device for enhanced security.
saving_vault_intro.passphrase_info: Adds a secret "25th word" to your vault: anyone who finds your 12 words alone cannot spend your funds, and the seed copy stored on this phone stays useless without it.
saving_vault_intro.passphrase_warning: ⚠ Losing the passphrase means irrecoverably losing your Hot Vault funds, even if you possess the 12-word seed phrase. It is case-sensitive and spaces count. You should be able to memorise it, and include it on your seed phrase paper.
saving_vault_intro.dice_added: ✓ Dice rolls added, mixed with your phone's randomness
saving_vault_intro.dice_advanced: Advanced: create your own entropy via your dice rolls 🎲
saving_vault_intro.seed_para_1: This phone creates a seed (12 words) to sign with. Back it up on paper and as a SeedQR, give your watch-only wallet its public key and check the first addresses match.
saving_vault_intro.seed_para_2: Then wipe the seed from this phone. To sign, scan the SeedQR: the seed is only held while you sign.
saving_vault_intro.seed_para_3: Keep this phone offline for good. If it ever connects to the internet, treat this seed as a hot wallet and plan to move your coins to a new seed.

withdraw_to_savings_vault.title: Coin Withdrawal
withdraw_to_savings_vault.explanation: The full pink bar represents the funds accumulated inside the Lightning Account. By clicking ‘Withdraw’ it will convert most of the funds into a real verifiable bitcoin ‘capsule’ (also known as a UTXO) filling one of the five slots in your Hot Vault, and leaving a small amount as pocket money for quick spending (Reserve Amount).

capsule_catalog.title: Capsule Cheat Sheet
capsule_catalog.intro_white: White capsules = small amounts (like pennies, nickels, quarters) - cost high fees relative to their size
capsule_catalog.intro_colored: Colored capsules = larger amounts of Bitcoin - cost lower fees relative to their size
capsule_catalog.fill_level: The fill level shows how full the capsule is within its tier.
capsule_catalog.fees_text: Just like spending quarters and pennies can be cumbersome, spending small-sized BTC capsules has its engineering friction in terms of fees. If you select lots of white capsules to spend from, your transaction gets bigger in terms of complexity which means higher fees.
capsule_catalog.privacy_text: There's also a privacy concern. Each capsule usually has its own history. If you use a large capsule to buy something small, your wallet will send the leftover back to you as a new "change capsule." This can sometimes suggest that you control a larger amount of Bitcoin.
capsule_catalog.rec_small: • Use small capsules for everyday payments
capsule_catalog.rec_large: • Keep larger capsules for long-term saving
capsule_catalog.rec_combine: • Occasionally combine small capsules when fees are low, unless you plan to spend them soon
capsule_catalog.rec_label: • Label your capsules when you receive them, especially KYC'd ones, so you can track and manage them strategically
capsule_catalog.kyc_warning: ⚠️ Never mix KYC and non-KYC capsules in the same transaction. Selecting a KYC capsule alongside a non-KYC one links them on-chain, compromising the privacy of your non-KYC coins.

seedqr_backup.copy_by_hand: You'll copy it by hand onto a {size}×{size} grid: a printed SeedQR template or a steel plate. It takes about 20 minutes. Then you scan your copy to check it.
seedqr_backup.intro: A SeedQR is your recovery phrase drawn as a QR code. With it you can sign by scanning instead of typing your words, and wallets like SeedSigner, Jade and Krux can read it too.

signing_safety.official_body: Install from the App Store or Google Play, never from a link someone sends you.

signing_safety.checklist_title: Checklist for the signing wallet's phone
signing_safety.why_body: A signature becomes public once the transaction is sent. A tampered signing app can hide pieces of your recovery phrase inside its signatures, and someone watching the blockchain can put them back together, sometimes from a single transaction. Keeping the signing phone offline doesn't stop this: the signature itself carries the leak.
signing_safety.offline_phone_body: This is for you. Example: an old phone, kept offline, runs Cypher Box in Offline Seed-Signer mode as your signing device: the seed lives on your SeedQR backups and is scanned in to sign. Your everyday phone holds a watch & broadcast only wallet made from the seed's public key: a Cypher Box Cold Vault, or another app such as Sparrow. It shows your balance, prepares transactions and broadcasts them once signed, but can't sign them.
signing_safety.offline_phone_title: Signing on an offline phone with Cypher Box
signing_safety.hardware_body: A device like a Coldcard or Jade signs, not a phone. The phone checklist below isn't for you. Just install the device's firmware only from its maker, through their own app or website.
signing_safety.hardware_title: Cold Vault signed by a hardware wallet
signing_safety.everyday_body: You send and receive with the Hot Vault on this phone. Nothing to do here.
signing_safety.everyday_title: Hot Vault as your everyday wallet

verify_tx_guide.mismatch_body: Don't send it. Go back and start the payment again. If a freshly signed transaction still doesn't match, stop using that signing device until you know why.
verify_tx_guide.fee_body: The coins going in, minus everything going out. It should be close to the fee you chose.
verify_tx_guide.change_body: Anything left over goes back to you: your own wallet, or the account you picked for change.
verify_tx_guide.amounts_body: The payment matches what you meant to send.
verify_tx_guide.recipients_body: Compare the whole address with the one you meant to pay, not just the first and last few characters. Scammers make look-alike addresses that match at both ends.
verify_tx_guide.coinbin_body: Download Coinbin, the open-source tool behind coinb.in, from its official GitHub page (github.com/OutCast3k/coinbin). Turn off Wi-Fi, open its index.html file in your browser, and paste the transaction into the Verify tab. Close the tab before you go back online.
verify_tx_guide.entropylab_body: Download entropylab.html from entropylab.online or its GitHub page (github.com/OogaBoogaX/entropylab), and check its SHA-256 matches the project's SHA256SUMS file. Turn off Wi-Fi, open the file in your browser, and paste the transaction into the PSBT Inspector under Transactions. Close the tab before you go back online.
verify_tx_guide.node_body: Run decoderawtransaction followed by the transaction, in a terminal with bitcoin-cli or in Bitcoin Core's Window → Console. Nothing leaves your machine.
verify_tx_guide.electrum_body: Turn off Wi-Fi first. Then Tools → Load transaction → From text, and paste.
verify_tx_guide.sparrow_body: File → Open Transaction → From Text, then paste. It decodes without an internet connection.
verify_tx_guide.step2_title: Step 2: Decode it with a tool you control
verify_tx_guide.step1_body: Tap {label} on the screen you came from. It only copies; nothing is sent. Other apps can read your clipboard, so when you are done, copy something else to replace it.
verify_tx_guide.no_seed: Checking a transaction never needs your seed phrase. Never type your seed into any tool for this.
verify_tx_guide.never_paste_body: A signed transaction shows which coins you own, who you are paying, how much, and where your change goes. A website you paste it into gets all of that, plus your IP address. Anyone holding a signed transaction can also broadcast it, until you spend those coins some other way.
verify_tx_guide.never_paste_title: Never paste it into a website while online
verify_tx_guide.device_screen: Your signing device's screen is the most important check: confirm the address and amount there. This guide is for a second opinion from a tool you control.
verify_tx_guide.need_usual: Usually not. Before you can swipe to send, Cypher Box checks that the signed transaction is exactly the one you approved, and shows you every amount and address in it.
verify_tx_guide.need_imported: It's worth it here. You opened a finished transaction, so Cypher Box has no record of what you meant to send and nothing to compare it with. It shows you every amount and address, but only you can tell whether they are right.
verify_tx_guide.title: Check your transaction yourself
